act1_quiz.prompt: Kampala sits on a series of hills drained by valley wetlands (Nakivubo, Lubigi, Kyetinda) at the tail of the March-May long rains. Which flood mechanism dominates here?
act1_quiz.hint: Think about what a single intense storm cell does over a hilly, built-up city.
options: Urban flash flooding: short, intense convective downpours shed off the hills and overwhelm drainage channels feeding the valley wetlands
Slow riverine flooding from a large main-stem river rising over several weeks
Coastal storm-surge flooding from Lake Victoria seiches
Snowmelt flooding from the Rwenzori mountains
act1_quiz.correct: Urban flash flooding: short, intense convective downpours shed off the hills and overwhelm drainage channels feeding the valley wetlands
act1_quiz.answer_note: Kampala has no large main-stem river through the city; its flood problem is pluvial. Runoff from impervious hillsides converges into low-lying valley channels and former wetlands, so a single high-intensity storm cell can flood settlements within hours.
act1_quiz.bn_purpose: Why the ensemble-mean rainfall can look benign while the tail signal carries the real flash-flood risk.

act1_quiz.prompt: Which exposure characteristic makes Kampala's low-lying neighbourhoods especially vulnerable when heavy rain is forecast?
act1_quiz.hint: Consider where informal housing has expanded and what used to occupy that land.
options: Informal settlements have encroached on the wetland buffers and drainage corridors, while silted and waste-blocked channels reduce the system's capacity
Most housing is built on high ridgelines far from any drainage path
The city's storm drains are oversized, so only dam failure poses a threat
Vulnerability is limited to the central business district's office towers
act1_quiz.correct: Informal settlements have encroached on the wetland buffers and drainage corridors, while silted and waste-blocked channels reduce the system's capacity
act1_quiz.answer_note: Papyrus wetlands like Nakivubo, Lubigi and Kyetinda once buffered storm runoff. Informal housing built in these basins, plus solid-waste blockage and silting of the primary channels, means even moderate forecast rainfall translates into high impact for the people living there.
act1_quiz.bn_purpose: Exposure context: why a localized-moderate spatial signal still warrants escalation when the exposed population sits in the drainage path.

decision.checkpoint_prompt: The ensemble mean may look benign but the tail signal is rising ahead of onset. What DOC level do you set, and why? A 'Watch + re-check + note the tail uncertainty' is a strong answer.

counterfactual.prompt: What if a precautionary no-regret action (alert city/district focal points, clear drainage and ready evacuation) were taken at the lead round on the tail signal?
counterfactual.narrative: Acting on a short-lead tail signal is exactly what the flood BN's tail_risk node exists to surface. The counterfactual illustrates loss reduction without claiming certainty.
